# Bootstrap Readiness Checklist: Finance-Dashboard Reuse Integration

**Purpose**: Check the requirements in spec, plan, research, data model and contracts for quality before `/speckit-tasks` / `/speckit-converge`. Covers config and naming, the auth/security boundary, the API contracts, and consistency between spec and plan.
**Created**: 2026-10-19
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md) · [research.md](../research.md) · [data-model.md](../data-model.md) · [contracts/](../contracts/)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Reviewer rules for this run**:
- New code must not mention `fh`, `finance-helper` or `finance-dashboard` (owner, 2026-10-19).
- Every deviation between spec and plan counts as a **conflict** that the spec must resolve. Recording it in the plan's Complexity Tracking is not enough.

## Configuration & Environment

- [ ] CHK017 Is `settings.py` editing treated the same way throughout FR5.3? The "Permitted" list allows config via `api/settings.py`. "Common Mistakes" #2 says editing `settings.py` needs pre-approval. [Conflict, Spec §FR5.3]
- [ ] CHK018 Are host-port variables defined for every service that worktrees isolate? The spec names `API_HOST_PORT`/`UI_HOST_PORT` only. `MCP_HOST_PORT` appears only in the configuration contract, so two worktrees would both claim port 9000. [Gap, Spec §FR6.5, contracts/configuration.md §Ports]
  - **Resolution (pending reviewer check):** Spec updated 2026-10-19: `MCP_HOST_PORT` added to FR2, FR6.5 and the config table.
- [ ] CHK019 Is the FR2 phrase "port bindings changed to `API_HOST_PORT` and `MELOS_COMPOSE_NAME`" clarified? `MELOS_COMPOSE_NAME` is a project name, not a port binding. [Clarity, Spec §FR2]
  - **Resolution (pending reviewer check):** Spec updated 2026-10-19: FR2 wording fixed.
- [ ] CHK020 Is the required/optional status of SMTP consistent? FR6.5 and the quickstart call SMTP optional in dev ("leave blank"). error-responses.md says the API fails on boot if any `SMTP_*` is missing. Assumption 3 says it "must be configured". [Conflict, Spec §FR6.5, §Assumptions 3, contracts/error-responses.md §SMTP]
  - **Resolution (pending reviewer check):** Owner decision 2026-10-19: dev has a real SMTP provider. Spec FR6.5, Assumption 3, quickstart and error-responses.md updated to the code's behaviour (503 `smtp_config_error` per request, no boot failure).
- [ ] CHK021 Is the behaviour defined when `MELOS_DATA` is set but empty, or when `SEED_DEV_USER=1` and the email or password is missing? The contract says "must not be empty" and "no silent defaults" but gives no failure mode. [Edge Case, contracts/configuration.md]
- [ ] CHK022 Is the version policy unambiguous? FR4 pins exact library versions but leaves `uv`, Node and npm at "Latest", and says Node is in `.node-version` "if present". [Ambiguity, Spec §FR4, §Tech Stack Summary]

## API Contracts (auth, kitchens, errors, health)

- [ ] CHK023 Is there one health shape across all docs? `health.md` forbids exposing versions. quickstart §3.1/§3.3 and T047 still specify `version` or a bare `{"status":"healthy"}`. [Conflict, contracts/health.md, quickstart §3, tasks T047]
  - **Resolution (pending reviewer check):** Owner decision 2026-10-19: no version field in any Docker config or `/health`; quickstart and error-responses.md updated. tasks.md T047 still says `version` (regenerate tasks).
- [ ] CHK024 Does the kitchen contract agree with itself on 403? §Access Control says "no endpoint returns 403", while PATCH, DELETE, member removal and invite creation document 403 for non-owners. Is the precedence stated: non-member → 404, member but not owner → 403? [Conflict, contracts/kitchen-membership-api.md]
  - **Resolution (pending reviewer check):** Owner decision 2026-10-19: 404 everywhere for non-members (reads and writes); 403 only `not_kitchen_owner`. Spec FR7 + contract §Access Control updated; code change is T113.
- [ ] CHK025 Do the kitchen/membership fields in the API contract match data-model.md? The contract has `description`, `updated_at`, `joined_at`. The data model has `is_archived`, `content_language`, `is_hidden`. Do PATCH/POST bodies include the optional `content_language` that the plan requires? [Conflict, contracts/kitchen-membership-api.md, data-model.md, Plan §Implementation outline 3]
- [ ] CHK026 Does the invite contract agree with data-model.md? The POST response returns the raw `token`/`invite_url`, but the data model says "raw token only ever in the email link". Expiry is called "hardcoded" yet shown as `INVITE_EXPIRY_DAYS`. Email is sent only "if guest's email is in the system". [Conflict, contracts/kitchen-membership-api.md §Invitations, data-model.md §kitchen_invite_tokens]
  - **Resolution (pending reviewer check):** Partly resolved 2026-10-19: contract now matches the code (create returns `status`/`template_kind`/`invite_id`, no raw token; 7-day TTL is a domain constant). Email-sending rule clarified: both new and existing invitees get an email. Field tables remain (T112).
- [ ] CHK027 Is the unauthenticated `POST /invites/accept` behaviour ("redirects to sign-up") defined in API terms, with a status code and body, and assigned to either the BFF or the API? [Clarity, contracts/kitchen-membership-api.md]
  - **Resolution (pending reviewer check):** Owner decision 2026-10-19: contract documents the code flow (public preview → accept with session or register with `invite_token`; 410; UI owns redirects). New invitees confirmed to get a `/signup?invite=` link.
- [ ] CHK028 Does the session table in auth-api.md (`session_id`, `token_hash`, `ip_address`) match data-model.md (`id`, `token unique`, no IP)? [Conflict, contracts/auth-api.md §Session Storage, data-model.md]
- [ ] CHK029 Is the `PageFetchFailed` status consistent? The mapping table says 502 and §External Service Errors says 400. Do bootstrap-scoped contracts mark the future-feature errors (`AIUnavailable`, `EmbeddingFailed`, …) as deferred? [Conflict, contracts/error-responses.md]
- [ ] CHK030 Is the BFF routing requirement precise? FR6 says `app/api/*` proxies to a FastAPI "`/api` backend", but the backend routes are unprefixed (`/auth/*`, `/kitchens`). [Ambiguity, Spec §FR6]
- [ ] CHK031 Is the module that enforces kitchen access named the same way everywhere? The contract says `application/kitchens.py`/`invites.py`. The plan and data model say `application/kitchen_access.py`. [Consistency, contracts/kitchen-membership-api.md, Plan §Constitution Check 3]
  - **Resolution (pending reviewer check):** Resolved 2026-10-19: contract names `application/kitchen_access.py`.

- [ ] CHK036 Are the failure and recovery requirements defined for the automatic `alembic upgrade head` on startup? This covers a DB that is not ready, a migration that fails partway, and whether the API container retries or exits. [Gap, Exception Flow, Spec §FR6.5 step 6]
- [ ] CHK037 Is the downgrade of migration `0002` safe once later revisions add vector columns, and is the rollback scope stated? `DROP EXTENSION vector` would fail or cascade. [Recovery, data-model.md §Migration 0002]
- [ ] CHK038 Is moving existing local data (old data dir, old `.env` keys) a requirement in the spec, and does it fit the no-finance-names rule if the instructions live in the README? [Gap, Recovery, quickstart §Bootstrap Acceptance Checks]
- [ ] CHK039 Are the leftover locale fields (`users.language`, `kitchen_invite_tokens.locale`, the read-only `melos_lang_cache`) defined in an English-only UI? This includes which values are written and why the lang cache key is kept at all. [Clarity, Spec §FR5.2, data-model.md, contracts/configuration.md]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`

- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
